chunks: Allah is sufficient as a Reckoner.
Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, said: "Indeed, Allah will make the people account for what they do."
And He said: "And your Lord is not unjust to the servants."

key_terms.ظَلَّامٍ: Unjust / One who deals with injustice
key_terms.وَكَيْلًا: A Reckoner / One who measures and accounts
key_terms.يُحَاسِبُ: He makes account / He holds to account

ai.seo_question: What Quranic verses does Kamal al-Din cite to describe Allah as a sufficient Reckoner?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes these verses to underscore the justice (*'adl*) of Allah, a cornerstone of Shia theology, affirming that the Divine Reckoner is perfectly just and not unjust to His servants. This narration reinforces the certainty of *Hisab* (accounting) on the Day of Judgment, linking divine omniscience with equitable judgment. The emphasis on Allah being 'sufficient' as a Reckoner highlights His self-sufficiency and authority in evaluating human deeds without need for external witnesses.
